description: This file contains utility functions related to Triton code generation within the PyTorch Inductor compiler. It manages argument signatures, type deductions, buffer alignments, and parameter metadata essential for kernel compilation and runtime execution in Triton backend integration.

methods.name: should_unwrap_unspec_arg(name: str)
methods.description: Determines if an argument should be unwrapped based on its name and device type; unwrapping is disabled for CPU devices and for mutated buffers not used as outputs.

methods.name: str signature_of(arg: KernelArgType, *, size_dtype: Optional[str])
methods.description: Infers the signature string for a given argument based on its type, dtype, and context, handling special cases like float8, size arguments, workspace, and TMA descriptors.

methods.name: non_constexpr_signature(signature)
methods.description: Filters out constexpr arguments from a signature list, returning only non-constexpr argument types.

methods.name: dict[str,str] signature_to_meta( signature: list[KernelArgType], *, size_dtype: Optional[str], argdefs: list[ArgName], indices: Optional[list[int]] = None, is_template: bool = False, )
methods.description: Converts a signature of arguments into a metadata dictionary mapping argument names to corresponding types, deciding types based on various conditions and configurations.

methods.name: is_unaligned_buffer(arg: TensorArg)
methods.description: Checks if a buffer argument is unaligned based on buffer layout and graph registration, which influences memory access optimizations.

methods.name: tuple[int,...] equal_1_arg_indices( args: list[KernelArgType], *, indices: Optional[list[int]] = None, )
methods.description: Returns indices of arguments that are equal to 1 based on static analysis, aiding in kernel signature generation.

methods.name: Any config_of( args: list[KernelArgType], *, indices: Optional[list[int]] = None, )
methods.description: Determines the configuration of arguments, especially their alignment status and whether they are equal to 1, which influences how kernels are generated.

methods.name: bool is_aligned(x: KernelArgType, alignment: int, include_tensor: bool)

ctags.name: is_aligned
ctags.pattern: /^    def is_aligned(x: KernelArgType, alignment: int, include_tensor: bool) -> bool:$/

ctags.name: signature_to_meta
ctags.signature: ( signature: list[KernelArgType], *, size_dtype: Optional[str], argdefs: list[ArgName], indices: Optional[list[int]] = None, is_template: bool = False, )
